pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence is wrong? (1 mark)
   A. I have an books.
   B. I have a book.
   C. I have books.
   D. I have the book.

2. Which article goes before 'hour'? (1 mark)
   A. no article always
   B. a
   C. an
   D. the

3. What does 'Haste makes waste' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Waste is good
   B. If you hurry, you may make mistakes and waste things
   C. Food is wasted at night
   D. Hurry is always best

4. /p/ is a whispered sound. /b/ is (1 mark)
   A. also whispered
   B. a vowel
   C. voiced, with a buzz
   D. silent

5. Which word best describes Neema in the passage? (1 mark)
   A. greedy
   B. honest
   C. rude
   D. lazy

6. Language patterns: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. We have enough chairs to sit on.
   B. We have chairs enough to sit on.
   C. We have enough chairs for sit.
   D. We have enough chair to sit on.

7. Which word has a silent h at the start? (1 mark)
   A. hour
   B. hen
   C. house
   D. hand

8. In the word 'hospital', which syllable is stressed? (1 mark)
   A. None
   B. The first
   C. The third
   D. The second

9. What punctuation mark follows the greeting 'Dear Achieng'? (1 mark)
   A. A full stop
   B. A colon
   C. A comma
   D. A question mark

10. In the five-finger test, four or five fingers on a page mean the book is (1 mark)
   A. too hard for now
   B. too easy
   C. empty
   D. just right

11. An adjective is a word that (1 mark)
   A. shows an action
   B. describes a noun
   C. joins sentences
   D. names a person

12. 'Steal' means to (1 mark)
   A. read a book
   B. take something that does not belong to you
   C. wash clothes
   D. give a gift

13. Dialogues: Which question is factual? (1 mark)
   A. Who wanted to talk to Grandmother?
   B. What lesson does the story teach?
   C. How do you think Achieng felt?
   D. Why do you think Baraka was excited?

14. A good title for a story about a boy who emails his grandmother is (1 mark)
   A. The Weather in April
   B. How to Bake Bread
   C. A Message for Grandmother
   D. A Trip to the Farm

15. Where can you find pictures for a composition? (1 mark)
   A. Only in a dictionary
   B. Only on money
   C. Only on a calendar
   D. Books, magazines and websites with a teacher's help

16. What is a stranger? (1 mark)
   A. A person who lives next door
   B. Your teacher
   C. A close friend
   D. A person you do not know

17. What are data bundles? (1 mark)
   A. Bundles of firewood
   B. An amount of internet you buy for a phone or computer
   C. Sheets of paper
   D. A kind of laptop

18. In the five-finger test, what does it mean if you use all five fingers on one page? (1 mark)
   A. The book is just right
   B. The book has good pictures
   C. The book is probably too hard for now
   D. The book is too easy

19. Choose the correct -ing form of 'play'. (1 mark)
   A. playying
   B. playing
   C. plaiing
   D. plaing

20. Which time word usually goes with the present progressive? (1 mark)
   A. in 2010
   B. last night
   C. at the moment
   D. yesterday

21. When do we write the word 'I' as a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. Always
   B. Only at the start of a sentence
   C. Only in names
   D. Never

22. What is a shed on a farm? (1 mark)
   A. A tool for digging
   B. A small building for tools or animals
   C. A person who works on a farm
   D. A kind of crop

23. Which word begins with /v/? (1 mark)
   A. window
   B. weed
   C. wheat
   D. vegetables

24. What should you do at a full stop when reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Speed up
   B. Shout
   C. Pause a little
   D. Skip the next word

25. What is rhythm in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. The name of the poet
   B. The beat in the words
   C. The number of pages
   D. The title of the poem

26. What is the contraction of 'they are'? (1 mark)
   A. thay're
   B. they're
   C. theyr'e
   D. they'er

27. Which sentence has a double negative that should be corrected? (1 mark)
   A. I don't have any pencils.
   B. I don't have no pencil.
   C. I don't have a pencil.
   D. I have no pencil.

28. What is a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. A description of an object
   B. A set of instructions
   C. A list of facts
   D. A story that tells what happened in order

29. What does 'prevention' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of food
   B. Acting so that something bad does not happen
   C. Medicine that cures an illness
   D. A sharp object

30. Which pair of words differs only in /h/ and /f/? (1 mark)
   A. hill and fill
   B. cat and cap
   C. ship and sheep
   D. sit and seat

31. In the story, why was Omondi standing alone? (1 mark)
   A. He had a football
   B. He had lost his shoes
   C. Other children refused to play with him because of his mother's illness
   D. He wanted to study

32. What is a clinic? (1 mark)
   A. A place where people get health care
   B. A place for playing football
   C. A market stall
   D. A school library

33. What does 'rinse' mean in the passage on hand washing? (1 mark)
   A. To hide germs
   B. To add soap
   C. To wash off soap with clean water
   D. To dry the hands

34. Which conjunction means the same as 'but' in 'The room was small, ____ it was very clean'? (1 mark)
   A. for
   B. nor
   C. so
   D. yet

35. What is athletics? (1 mark)
   A. Only football
   B. A type of food
   C. Sports such as running, jumping and throwing
   D. A kind of card game

36. Which sentence has the /ð/ sound in the first word? (1 mark)
   A. Think before you act.
   B. The team practised hard.
   C. Three players scored.
   D. Thank the coach.

37. Which question has the correct word order after 'where'? (1 mark)
   A. Where you do keep the ball?
   B. Where you keep the ball?
   C. Where do you keeps the ball?
   D. Where do you keep the ball?

38. Which is the negative of 'I have eaten'? (1 mark)
   A. I do not have eaten.
   B. I not have eaten.
   C. I has not eaten.
   D. I have not eaten.

39. Which word has a silent k? (1 mark)
   A. knee
   B. key
   C. kind
   D. king

40. Why is it good to read a newspaper regularly? (1 mark)
   A. It replaces school
   B. You learn what is happening and new words
   C. It gives you money
   D. It cannot teach anything

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Compose a tongue twister with at least six words that contain the sound /w/. (3 marks)

42. Write an introduction of two sentences for the topic 'A day I enjoyed'. (2 marks)

43. List the five parts of a friendly letter. (3 marks)

44. Sort these adverbs into manner, time and place: quietly, later, nearby, always, neatly, upstairs. (3 marks)

45. Give two examples of regular plurals and two of irregular plurals. (2 marks)

46. Write a diary entry of about 60 words about a day at school. Include the date, feelings and a plan for tomorrow. (5 marks)

47. List three places where we use a capital letter. (3 marks)

48. Write two sentences using 'compose' and 'reply'. (2 marks)

49. Explain two ways to make a story interesting. (4 marks)

50. Correct: (a) 'How much books are there?' (b) 'I do not have some money.' (2 marks)

51. Name the three parts of fluent reading and explain each briefly. (3 marks)

52. Write a narrative of about 60 words about a visit to a farm. Include a beginning, a middle, an end and a simile. (5 marks)

53. Give two reasons why we should read widely. (2 marks)

54. Use when, where, who and whose in four questions about a sports day. (4 marks)

55. Explain the difference between a fact and an opinion. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

56. Explain how you can feel the difference between /t/ and /d/ using your throat. (2 marks)

57. Write a question for each answer: (a) 'It is at the stadium.' (b) 'The coach.' (2 marks)

58. Give the meaning of clan, ancestor and adopt. (3 marks)

59. Explain the rule for changing nouns that end in y into plurals. Give two examples. (3 marks)

60. Explain the difference between 'it's' and 'its' with one sentence for each. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — I have an books.
   A and an cannot be used before a plural noun.

2. C — an
   The h is silent, so hour starts with a vowel sound.

3. B — If you hurry, you may make mistakes and waste things
   Rushing often leads to errors.

4. C — voiced, with a buzz
   The difference between p and b is the voice.

5. B — honest
   She returned the purse and refused a reward.

6. A — We have enough chairs to sit on.
   The pattern is enough + noun + to + verb.

7. A — hour
   Hour begins with a vowel sound, so the h is silent.

8. B — The first
   We say HOS-pi-tal.

9. C — A comma
   A comma follows the greeting.

10. A — too hard for now
   Many unknown words show that it is too hard.

11. B — describes a noun
   Adjectives describe nouns.

12. B — take something that does not belong to you
   Stealing is taking what is not yours.

13. A — Who wanted to talk to Grandmother?
   The answer is written in the text.

14. C — A Message for Grandmother
   It suits the story.

15. D — Books, magazines and websites with a teacher's help
   There are many safe sources.

16. D — A person you do not know
   A stranger is someone you do not know.

17. B — An amount of internet you buy for a phone or computer
   Data bundles are bought to use the internet.

18. C — The book is probably too hard for now
   Five unknown words on a page suggests the book is too hard.

19. B — playing
   A verb ending in y keeps the y before -ing.

20. C — at the moment
   'At the moment' shows an action happening now.

21. A — Always
   'I' is always a capital.

22. B — A small building for tools or animals
   A shed is used for storing tools or sheltering animals.

23. D — vegetables
   'Vegetables' begins with /v/, said with the top teeth on the lower lip.

24. C — Pause a little
   A full stop tells the reader to pause.

25. B — The beat in the words
   Rhythm is the pattern of beats.

26. B — they're
   The apostrophe replaces the a in 'are'.

27. B — I don't have no pencil.
   Use only one negative word.

28. D — A story that tells what happened in order
   A narrative tells events in order.

29. B — Acting so that something bad does not happen
   Prevention stops problems before they start.

30. A — hill and fill
   'Hill' begins with /h/ and 'fill' with /f/.

31. C — Other children refused to play with him because of his mother's illness
   The other children were afraid because they did not know the facts.

32. A — A place where people get health care
   Clinics give health care.

33. C — To wash off soap with clean water
   You rinse after soap.

34. D — yet
   'Yet' shows a surprise, like 'but'.

35. C — Sports such as running, jumping and throwing
   Athletics includes track and field events.

36. B — The team practised hard.
   'The' has voiced 'th'; 'think', 'three' and 'thank' have unvoiced 'th'.

37. D — Where do you keep the ball?
   The helping verb 'do' comes before the subject.

38. D — I have not eaten.
   Add not after have.

39. A — knee
   In 'knee' the k is not pronounced.

40. B — You learn what is happening and new words
   Regular reading builds knowledge and vocabulary.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: We watched worms wriggle when the wind whistled.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a sentence, 1 for at least six /w/ words, 1 for making sense.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: It was a sunny Sunday in Kisumu. My family went to the lake for a picnic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for when or where and 1 mark for who or what.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Address, date, greeting, body, closing and name (address and date may be given together).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for address and date, 1 mark for greeting and body, 1 mark for closing and name.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Manner: quietly, neatly. Time: later, always. Place: nearby, upstairs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Regular: books, dishes. Irregular: men, feet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: An entry in the first person with a date, events in order, feelings, a plan and a sign-off.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the date, 1 for events in order, 1 for feelings, 1 for a plan, 1 for correct tense and punctuation.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence; the word I; names of people; names of places; days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: I will compose an email to my uncle. He will reply tomorrow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Start with something that makes the reader curious, and add small details or similes. These help the reader picture the story and want to continue.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each way explained.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) How many books are there? (b) I do not have any money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Accuracy: reading the words correctly. Speed: reading at a comfortable, not rushed pace. Expression: using the voice to show meaning and feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part explained.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: A story of about 60 words in the past tense with clear parts and a simile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the beginning, 1 for events in order, 1 for the end, 1 for a simile, 1 for correct tense and punctuation.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: It builds vocabulary and improves reading speed and understanding. It gives knowledge and enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: When is sports day? Where is it held? Who is the guest of honour? Whose team is winning?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: A fact can be checked, for example 'Germs are tiny'. An opinion says what someone thinks, for example 'Cold water is nicest'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each definition and 1 for examples.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put your fingers on your throat and say the sounds. You feel a buzz with /d/ because it is voiced, but no buzz with /t/, which is whispered.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the buzz with /d/, 1 mark for no buzz with /t/.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) Where is it? (b) Who is the man with the whistle?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable question.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: A clan is a large group of families with the same ancestor. An ancestor is a family member who lived long ago. To adopt is to take a child into your family and raise the child as your own.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: If a consonant comes before y, change y to i and add es (baby, babies). If a vowel comes before y, add s (boy, boys).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for correct examples.

60. (4 marks)
   Answer: It's means 'it is' or 'it has': It's raining. Its shows belonging: The dog wagged its tail.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each correct sentence.
